title: Knickerbocker Glory
subtitle: Layered sundae glass of ice cream, fruit, cream, and sauce
excerpt: The quintessential British ice cream sundae, layers of fresh fruit, vanilla ice cream, a sharp raspberry sauce, and whipped cream in a tall glass. No fixed recipe; the pleasure is in the assembly.
sourceNotes: The knickerbocker glory appeared on British café menus from the 1930s and became a fixture of seaside and high-street ice cream parlours through the mid-20th century. The name is thought to derive from 'Knickerbocker' as a term for a New Yorker, though the dish became quintessentially British rather than American in character. There is no canonical recipe, the format is a tall glass, layers, and abundance.

recipe.yieldDescription: Serves 2–4 (scales to the number of glasses)
recipe.makeAheadNotes: The raspberry sauce can be made up to 3 days ahead and kept covered in the fridge. Assemble the glasses just before serving.

content.text: A knickerbocker glory is an ice cream sundae served in a tall glass, layers of fresh fruit, scoops of vanilla ice cream, a sharp raspberry sauce, and softly whipped cream, finished with toasted flaked almonds and eaten immediately with a long spoon. There is no strict recipe; the format is tall, layered, and generous. Use the best vanilla ice cream you can find or make, the Vanilla Ice Cream recipe on this site works well here.

items.prepNote: to thin and sharpen the sauce

content.text: Warm the raspberry jam and lemon juice together in a small saucepan over a low heat, stirring until combined and runny. Add the fresh raspberries and stir briefly, the raspberries will break down slightly into the sauce. Pass through a fine sieve if you want a smooth sauce, or leave as-is for a slightly textured version with visible raspberry seeds. Leave to cool. The sauce can be made up to 3 days ahead.

Whip the double cream with the icing sugar to soft peaks, it should hold its shape but remain silky and not stiff. Transfer to a piping bag fitted with a star nozzle if you want a neat finish, or simply spoon.

Work quickly once you start assembling, the ice cream will melt. Into each tall glass, layer the fruit first: a few halved strawberries around the inside of the glass so they show through. Add a spoonful of raspberry sauce, then a generous scoop of vanilla ice cream, then more fruit, then another scoop of ice cream. Drizzle sauce over the top layer of ice cream. Pipe or spoon a generous amount of whipped cream on top, scatter the toasted flaked almonds over the cream, and serve immediately with long-handled spoons.

items.symptom: Ice cream melts before the assembly is finished
items.cause: The glasses were warm, or the assembly took too long.
items.fix: Chill the glasses in the freezer for 10 minutes before assembling. Have all components ready before you start, fruit hulled, sauce made, cream whipped, almonds toasted.

items.symptom: Sauce is too sweet and cloying
items.cause: Raspberry jam is already sweet, and the balance needs the lemon juice to cut through it.
items.fix: Add lemon juice a teaspoon at a time and taste until the sauce has a sharp, fruity edge rather than a flat jam sweetness.

items.cause: The cream was whipped to stiff peaks and then collapsed, or was under-whipped.
items.fix: Whip to soft peaks, the cream should hold its shape gently. Stiff peaks will set, then weep. Use cold cream from the fridge and whip in a cold bowl for the best stability.

content.text: The assembled knickerbocker glory must be eaten immediately. The sauce keeps in the fridge for up to 3 days, covered. The whipped cream can be prepared up to an hour ahead and refrigerated.
